newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom sell-off set for May.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom sell-off set for May.

text.p: France Telecom, the world's fourth largest telecommunications operator, is to be partially privatised in May, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
"I can confirm that the flotation will be in May... for at least 25 billion francs. But there is no decision on the calendar," he said.
Financial newspaper La Tribune said on Wednesday that a six-day public offer of shares in France Telecom was due to start on May 20, with stock trading to begin in early June.
The advertising agency handling the campaign for the sale said the campaign would begin in the week of May 1 and run for over three weeks.
The sale is due to be made in two tranches, with no date fixed for the second tranche offering.
Government officials at the finance ministry were not available for comment on the report.

An executive at advertising agency Alice, appointed in January to handle the campaign aimed at the general public with a budget of 75 million francs, told Reuters it planned to present a friendly image of the company to encourage the sale.
"We are aiming to persuade by emotions rather than by reason," he said. "It is not the first privatisation, and it is a very major company. We will play the likeable card," he added.
The campaign is expected to announce a price range for the offering in its last week, La Tribune said.
"But the definitive price will not be made public before the end of May," the newspaper said.

"From the close of the offer, the government will have eight days to determine the price of the share. The finance ministry will base (its decision) on the breadth of demand and on the valuation of the company, which should be set at the end of May by the Privatisation Commission."
Brokerage firm BZW has valued France Telecom at 147 billion francs, but the Tribune said Merrill Lynch, which is advising France Telecom, has set a higher valuation.

It said the valuation is complicated by a multitude of exceptional items in the company's 1996 accounts, including a downward revision of its property holdings to 38 billion francs from 82 billion and a one-time transfer of 37.5 billion francs to the French state to cover pension liabilities. The newspaper said the government is counting on the offer to increase the number of individual shareholders in France -- currently around 5.1 million.
"In sum, the sale of 20 percent of France Telecom, which would generate around 25 billion francs for the state, could touch...six million French people," the newspaper said.

The government also needs to raise funds through the sale of France Telecom shares and other privatisations to pay for capital injections into struggling state-owned companies, including French bank Credit Lyonnais.
